quote: It would be correct to say that the use of machines tends to weaken men's bodies, but not their minds.

The use, therefore, of machines, instead of weakening the capacities of men, really strengthens them; for it not only keeps them in practice, but it calls for the exercise of more strength and skill than is required for the use of their naked hands.
note: machines demand more bodily strength and skill

quote: Reliing on machines does not weaken human capacities.
In the end the greater the mechanical contrivances become the more and more dependent is the race of Man upon them.
The use of machines does not weaken the human faculties, because the work of machines is performed by the human brain.
Men are not injured by the use of machines, but are benefited by them.
note: machines cannot do thinking, so those capacities untouched

quote: The more machines we invent, the more machines we employ, the less intelligent and human we shall become.
If we installed machines and depended upon them, we would gradually lose our human faculties and abilities and become mere machines.
So far as a machine can be made to do the work of man, it is a hindrance to the development and use of his faculties.
the more we rely on machines to help us remember, the more our memories are weakened
Thus the very machines which are supposed to be harmless, are proving themselves to be the cause of the deterioration of the race.
note: machines cause unemployment, which weakens the body

quote: the development of the mechanical arts in conjunction with the development of the social arts and the development of science, has had an enormous influence in increasing human capacities
note: mechanical arts train the mind to accuracy and educate faculties

quote: But the race which becomes dependent on machines will be weakened, and the individuals who cannot get machines will be less well off than those who can get them.
Using machines does not weaken us; it helps us.
It is true that the invention of machines weakened man's physical capacities, but it is also true that the invention of machines strengthened man's spiritual capacities.
So machinery to those who use it, increases their powers; but to those who do not use it, it only increases their helplessness and their dependence upon others.
Those who hold the former opinion are right.
note: machines are not living, so unreliable

quote: the less the machine has to do, the better the worker.
It is a matter of opinion, but the latter view is more likely to be true.
note: comparison of peoples' histories with machinery
